item.title: Crypto & Wartime Computing
item.description:
Secrecy as a workload — why breaking ciphers outran gears and relays and pulled computing into electronics. Thin index; doors live in the posts.

  1. Relays and Electromechanical Logic — binary logic in moving metal, and why metal is slow
  2. Wartime Crypto — Enigma, Bletchley, Colossus; named people; the urgency
  3. The Vacuum Tube Era — electronic switching without mechanical contacts
  4. Why the Transistor Had to Happen — tubes win speed, then hit heat/power/failure

Back to all paths.

item.title: Who Runs the Internet
item.description:
Who names numbers, names, and encodings — and what protocol story those registries sit on. Thin index; not an org catalog.

  1. ARPANET and Packet Switching — the research network that proved packets
  2. Ethernet and the Local Area Network — local link standardization (IEEE 802 kin)
  3. TCP/IP and the Modern Internet Stack — how heterogeneous nets become one internetwork
  4. Who Decides the Wire — RFCs / IETF / IANA / ICANN / RIRs / Unicode as seeds of a kind

Back to all paths.

item.title: Find, Then Talk
item.description:
Information retrieval and peer communication as one arc — then the consumer packaging of both. Thin index.

  1. TCP/IP and the Modern Internet Stack — the transport the apps rode
  2. Usenet, Archie, Gopher, and the Pre-Web Internet — find + talk → IRC → portals (Yahoo as seed)
  3. Google’s Big Data Infrastructure — the same category of find, at crawler scale

Back to all paths.

item.title: Privacy / Identity / Consent
item.description:
Protection, cryptography on a public network, identity protocols, and adversarial systems — engineering evolution, not a policy pamphlet. Thin index.

  1. Virtual Memory and Multitasking — isolation as a hardware/OS boundary
  2. Containers and Modern OS Isolation — namespaces and cgroups as shared-kernel boundaries
  3. Wartime Crypto — secrecy under a dedicated adversary (contrast with the open net)
  4. Privacy, Consent, Identity, Cyber — Saltzer/Schroeder → public-key → auth/consent → cyber as feedback
  5. Who Decides the Wire — shared identifiers the privacy layer still depends on

Back to all paths.

item.title: Visions That Shipped
item.description:
Forward links out of the journey — seeds of kinds that turned stack into lived platforms. Not biographies. Thin index.

  1. The GNU Movement and Linux — Stallman, Torvalds, and the commons under modern servers
  2. Visions That Shipped — Cisco, Gates, Jobs, GNU+Linus, Bezos, Musk as seeds; derive kin; stop
  3. Platform Synthesis — one high-level stop: distributed systems + networking + AI infra + privacy + software engineering

Back to all paths.
